title: 2 Corinthians Chapter 6 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on 2 Corinthians chapter 6 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: 2 Corinthians Chapter 6 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of 2 Corinthians Chapter 6.

questions.question: In 2 Corinthians 6, which of the following appears FIRST in the chapter?
options: We then, as workers together with him, beseech you also that ye receive not the grace of God in vain
Giving no offence in any thing, that the ministry be not blamed
In stripes, in imprisonments, in tumults, in labours, in watchings, in fastings
By pureness, by knowledge, by longsuffering, by kindness, by the Holy Ghost, by love unfeigned
questions.correctAnswer: We then, as workers together with him, beseech you also that ye receive not the grace of God in vain
questions.explanation: This statement is found in 2 Corinthians 6:1, which is the first verse of the chapter.

questions.question: According to 2 Corinthians 6:2, what has God said about the time of salvation?
options: Now is the accepted time; behold, now is the day of salvation
Salvation comes only to the chosen
The time of salvation is far off
questions.correctAnswer: Now is the accepted time; behold, now is the day of salvation
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 6:2 states, 'behold, now is the accepted time; behold, now is the day of salvation.'

questions.question: What are workers together with God beseeching you not to do according to 2 Corinthians 6:1?
options: Receive not the grace of God in vain
questions.correctAnswer: Receive not the grace of God in vain
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 6:1 says, 'We then, as workers together with him, beseech you also that ye receive not the grace of God in vain.'

questions.question: According to 2 Corinthians 6:3, what should ministers avoid in order that the ministry not be blamed?
options: Giving no offence in any thing
questions.correctAnswer: Giving no offence in any thing
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 6:3 states, 'Giving no offence in any thing, that the ministry be not blamed.'

questions.question: In 2 Corinthians 6:4, how do ministers approve themselves?
options: In much patience, in afflictions, in necessities, in distresses
questions.correctAnswer: In much patience, in afflictions, in necessities, in distresses
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 6:4 says, 'But in all things approving ourselves as the ministers of God, in much patience, in afflictions, in necessities, in distresses.'

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT listed in 2 Corinthians 6:5 as something ministers endure?
questions.correctAnswer: In riches
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 6:5 lists stripes, imprisonments, tumults, labours, watchings, and fastings but does not mention riches.

questions.question: According to 2 Corinthians 6:6, which of these is a quality ministers exhibit?
questions.correctAnswer: By pureness
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 6:6 includes 'By pureness, by knowledge, by longsuffering, by kindness, by the Holy Ghost, by love unfeigned.'

questions.question: According to 2 Corinthians 6:5, ministers endure which of the following?
questions.correctAnswer: Labours
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 6:5 states ministers endure 'in labours' among other hardships.

questions.question: What does 2 Corinthians 6:6 say ministers are characterized by, besides pureness and knowledge?
questions.correctAnswer: Longsuffering
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 6:6 lists 'by pureness, by knowledge, by longsuffering' as qualities of ministers.

questions.question: Which of these is mentioned in 2 Corinthians 6:5 as a hardship faced by ministers?
questions.correctAnswer: Watchings
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 6:5 includes 'in watchings' as one of the hardships ministers endure.

questions.question: According to 2 Corinthians 6:4, ministers approve themselves as ministers of God by what means?
options: In much patience, in afflictions, in necessities, in distresses
questions.correctAnswer: In much patience, in afflictions, in necessities, in distresses
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 6:4 states ministers approve themselves 'in much patience, in afflictions, in necessities, in distresses.'

questions.question: True or False: 2 Corinthians 6:2 says God has heard us in a time accepted.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 6:2 says, 'For he saith, I have heard thee in a time accepted.'

questions.question: True or False: According to 2 Corinthians 6:6, ministers show kindness and love unfeigned.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 6:6 says ministers exhibit 'by kindness, by the Holy Ghost, by love unfeigned.'

questions.question: True or False: 2 Corinthians 6 says ministers gain their ministry through political power.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: The text does not mention political power; instead it describes patience, affliction, and purity as characteristics of ministers (2 Corinthians 6:4-6).

questions.question: True or False: 2 Corinthians 6 says ministers avoid troubles and live in comfort.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 6:4-5 lists many hardships ministers endure, such as afflictions, imprisonments, and fastings, so they do not live in comfort.

medium.title: 2 Corinthians Chapter 6 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from 2 Corinthians Chapter 6 to real-life situations.

questions.question: According to 2 Corinthians 6:7, by what means is righteousness described as being on the right hand and on the left?
options: By the word of truth, by the power of God, by the armour of righteousness
By faith, by hope, by love
By prayer, by fasting, by patience
By works, by grace, by mercy
questions.correctAnswer: By the word of truth, by the power of God, by the armour of righteousness
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 6:7 states that righteousness is by the word of truth, by the power of God, and by the armour of righteousness on the right hand and on the left.

questions.question: What does 2 Corinthians 6:8 promise will happen if someone endures both honour and dishonour as described in 2 Corinthians 6:7?
options: They will be accepted by all men
They will be recognized as true despite being deceivers
They will be free from affliction
questions.correctAnswer: They will be recognized as true despite being deceivers
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 6:8 explains that by enduring honour and dishonour, evil report and good report, they are as deceivers yet true, connecting the endurance mentioned in 6:7 with authentic faithfulness.

questions.question: How does 2 Corinthians 6:9 describe the paradoxical condition of the ministers?
options: As unknown, and yet well known; as dying, and, behold, we live
As rich, and yet poor; as joyful, and yet sorrowful
As strong, and yet weak; as free, and yet bound
As wise, and yet foolish; as healed, and yet sick
questions.correctAnswer: As unknown, and yet well known; as dying, and, behold, we live
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 6:9 states these paradoxes directly, describing the ministers as unknown yet well known, dying yet living.

questions.question: How do 2 Corinthians 6:9 and 6:10 together illustrate the enduring spirit of the ministers?
options: By showing they are sorrowful yet always rejoicing and dying yet living
By indicating they are wealthy and famous
By suggesting they avoid afflictions and hardships
By emphasizing their separation from believers
questions.correctAnswer: By showing they are sorrowful yet always rejoicing and dying yet living
questions.explanation: Verse 6:9 describes them as dying yet living, and 6:10 continues with sorrowful yet always rejoicing, illustrating a spirit that endures despite hardships.

questions.question: What practical lesson about Christian integrity can be drawn from enduring both honour and dishonour as mentioned in 2 Corinthians 6:8?
options: Faithfulness involves maintaining truth despite opposition
Avoid all conflict to keep reputation
Only seek good reports from others
questions.correctAnswer: Faithfulness involves maintaining truth despite opposition
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 6:8 shows that believers may be honored or dishonored, yet must remain true, teaching practical integrity through perseverance.

questions.question: According to 2 Corinthians 6:10, how can one be poor yet make many rich?
options: By sharing spiritual riches and blessings
By accumulating wealth and donating it
questions.correctAnswer: By sharing spiritual riches and blessings
questions.explanation: The verse describes a spiritual paradox where possessing little materially but enriching others spiritually is emphasized.

questions.question: What does Paul mean in 2 Corinthians 6:11 when he says, 'our mouth is open unto you, our heart is enlarged'?
options: He is expressing openness and readiness to communicate freely
He is declaring victory over enemies
He is commanding silence and obedience
He is expressing sorrow and regret
questions.correctAnswer: He is expressing openness and readiness to communicate freely
questions.explanation: The verse uses metaphorical language to convey Paul’s willingness to speak openly and lovingly to the Corinthians.

questions.question: What does 2 Corinthians 6:12 suggest about the Corinthians’ restraint in receiving Paul’s message?
questions.correctAnswer: They are self-restrained, not Paul
questions.explanation: The verse states that the Corinthians are not straitened in Paul, but they are straitened in their own bowels, meaning they are inwardly constrained.

questions.question: How does 2 Corinthians 6:4 describe the character needed for ministry in difficult circumstances?
options: Much patience in afflictions, necessities, and distresses
questions.correctAnswer: Much patience in afflictions, necessities, and distresses
questions.explanation: The verse emphasizes patience and steadfastness under hardship as marks of faithful ministry.

questions.question: According to 2 Corinthians 6:5, which of the following is NOT mentioned as a hardship endured by the ministers?
questions.correctAnswer: In famines
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 6:5 lists stripes, imprisonments, tumults, labours, watchings, and fastings, but not famines.

questions.question: What qualities does 2 Corinthians 6:6 mention that ministers approve themselves by?
options: Pureness, knowledge, longsuffering, kindness, the Holy Ghost, love unfeigned
questions.correctAnswer: Pureness, knowledge, longsuffering, kindness, the Holy Ghost, love unfeigned
questions.explanation: The verse clearly lists these qualities as marks of approved ministry.

questions.question: How does 2 Corinthians 6:1 urge believers to respond to the grace of God?
options: Do not receive it in vain
questions.correctAnswer: Do not receive it in vain
questions.explanation: The verse exhorts believers to receive God's grace seriously and not in vain.

questions.question: What is the significance of the phrase 'behold, now is the accepted time; behold, now is the day of salvation' in 2 Corinthians 6:2?
options: It emphasizes the urgency of accepting salvation now
It refers to a future time for repentance
It suggests indefinite delay is acceptable
questions.correctAnswer: It emphasizes the urgency of accepting salvation now
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 6:2 highlights the present moment as the time to receive salvation.

questions.question: True or False: According to 2 Corinthians 6:10, the ministers are described as always sorrowful and never rejoicing.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 6:10 says they are sorrowful, yet always rejoicing, showing a balance of emotions.

questions.question: True or False: 2 Corinthians 6:3 commands that the ministry give no offence in anything so that the ministry is not blamed.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 6:3 explicitly instructs giving no offence in anything to avoid blame.

hard.title: 2 Corinthians Chapter 6 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from 2 Corinthians Chapter 6.

questions.question: What does Paul encourage the Corinthians to do in 2 Corinthians 6:13?
questions.correctAnswer: Be ye also enlarged
questions.explanation: This answer is correct as it directly quotes 2 Corinthians 6:13, where Paul speaks to the Corinthians as his children and encourages them to be enlarged.

questions.question: According to 2 Corinthians 6:14, what should believers not do?
options: Be unequally yoked together with unbelievers
questions.correctAnswer: Be unequally yoked together with unbelievers
questions.explanation: This is the correct answer as it is directly stated in 2 Corinthians 6:14, warning against the unequal yoking with unbelievers.

questions.question: What does 2 Corinthians 6:15 ask about the relationship between Christ and Belial?
options: What concord hath Christ with Belial?
What part hath he that believeth with an infidel?
What fellowship hath righteousness with unrighteousness?
What agreement hath the temple of God with idols?
questions.correctAnswer: What concord hath Christ with Belial?
questions.explanation: This question is answered directly in 2 Corinthians 6:15, highlighting the contrast between Christ and Belial.

questions.question: In 2 Corinthians 6:16, what does Paul say believers are the temple of?
questions.correctAnswer: The living God
questions.explanation: This is the correct answer as stated in 2 Corinthians 6:16, where Paul emphasizes that believers are the temple of the living God.

questions.question: What command does the Lord give in 2 Corinthians 6:17?
questions.correctAnswer: All of the above
questions.explanation: All options reflect the commands given in 2 Corinthians 6:17, where the Lord instructs to be separate and not touch the unclean.

questions.question: What does God promise to those who are separate in 2 Corinthians 6:18?
options: They shall be my sons and daughters
questions.correctAnswer: They shall be my sons and daughters
questions.explanation: This answer is correct as it is a direct quote from 2 Corinthians 6:18, where God promises to be a Father to those who separate themselves.

questions.question: What does the Greek word 'yoked' in 2 Corinthians 6:14 mean?
questions.correctAnswer: To join together
questions.explanation: The Greek word for 'yoked' refers to joining two animals together for work, indicating the idea of partnership or connection, as seen in 2 Corinthians 6:14.

questions.question: Which literary device is used in 2 Corinthians 6:14 regarding fellowship?
questions.correctAnswer: Antithesis
questions.explanation: Antithesis is the correct answer as Paul contrasts righteousness with unrighteousness and light with darkness in 2 Corinthians 6:14.

questions.question: Which Old Testament passage connects to the theme of being the temple of God in 2 Corinthians 6:16?
questions.correctAnswer: Ezekiel 37:27
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 37:27 connects as it emphasizes God's dwelling among His people, similar to 2 Corinthians 6:16 where believers are called the temple of God.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage echoes the call to come out and be separate from 2 Corinthians 6:17?
questions.correctAnswer: Revelation 18:4
questions.explanation: Revelation 18:4 echoes the call to come out from among them and be separate, aligning with the message in 2 Corinthians 6:17.

questions.question: What comes directly before 2 Corinthians 6:18?
questions.correctAnswer: 2 Corinthians 6:17
questions.explanation: The correct answer is 2 Corinthians 6:17, as it precedes verse 18, providing context for God's promise in verse 18.

questions.question: In 2 Corinthians 6:10, what paradox does Paul present about his condition?
options: As poor, yet making many rich
questions.correctAnswer: All of the above
questions.explanation: This answer is correct as 2 Corinthians 6:10 contains multiple paradoxes, highlighting the contrasts in Paul's ministry.

questions.question: The phrase 'I have heard thee in a time accepted' in 2 Corinthians 6:2 emphasizes what aspect of God's character?
questions.correctAnswer: His timing
questions.explanation: This answer is correct as 2 Corinthians 6:2 emphasizes God's perfect timing in responding to His people's needs.

questions.question: True or False: Paul encourages the Corinthians to remain in fellowship with those who do not believe.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: This is false as 2 Corinthians 6:14 clearly instructs believers not to be unequally yoked with unbelievers.

questions.question: True or False: In 2 Corinthians 6:11, Paul opens his heart to the Corinthians.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: This is true as 2 Corinthians 6:11 states that Paul's mouth is open and his heart is enlarged towards the Corinthians.

theological.title: 2 Corinthians Chapter 6 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from 2 Corinthians Chapter 6 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine does 2 Corinthians 6:2 teach about salvation?
options: Salvation is available only after death
Salvation is offered at a specific appointed time
Salvation is a future event only
Salvation is exclusively for the Jews
questions.correctAnswer: Salvation is offered at a specific appointed time
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 6:2 states, 'now is the accepted time; behold, now is the day of salvation,' emphasizing the immediacy and present availability of salvation.

questions.question: What doctrine about Christian ministry does 2 Corinthians 6:4 teach?
options: Ministers should seek comfort and avoid affliction
Ministers are to approve themselves through patience and endurance in trials
Ministers have no responsibility before God
Ministers should only preach in times of peace
questions.correctAnswer: Ministers are to approve themselves through patience and endurance in trials
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 6:4 teaches that ministers demonstrate their legitimacy by enduring afflictions and necessities with patience, showing the nature of faithful ministry.

questions.question: What doctrine about the believer's identity does 2 Corinthians 6:16 teach?
options: Believers are temporary dwellings of God
Believers are the temple of the living God where God dwells permanently
Believers must physically rebuild the temple
questions.correctAnswer: Believers are the temple of the living God where God dwells permanently
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 6:16 explicitly states that believers are the temple of the living God, in whom God dwells and walks, illustrating their sanctified identity.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does 2 Corinthians 6:6 specifically demonstrate?
questions.correctAnswer: Longsuffering
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 6:6 lists 'longsuffering' as a characteristic by which ministers approve themselves, reflecting God's attribute of patience with humanity.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is highlighted in 2 Corinthians 6:18?
questions.correctAnswer: Covenant faithfulness
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 6:18 quotes God promising to be a Father and the believers to be His sons and daughters, demonstrating His covenant faithfulness.

questions.question: How does 2 Corinthians 6:14-15 connect to the broader biblical theme of holiness and separation?
options: It encourages believers to coexist with all people irrespective of faith
It commands believers to separate from unbelievers because of fundamental spiritual incompatibility
It suggests that righteousness and unrighteousness can coexist harmoniously
It promotes syncretism for social unity
questions.correctAnswer: It commands believers to separate from unbelievers because of fundamental spiritual incompatibility
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 6:14-15 contrasts righteousness with unrighteousness and light with darkness, reinforcing the biblical call to holiness and separation found in Leviticus 20:7-8.

questions.question: In what way does 2 Corinthians 6:1-2 prepare for the New Testament emphasis on urgency in evangelism?
options: It denies any urgency in receiving grace
It emphasizes that now is the accepted time for salvation, urging immediate response
It postpones salvation to an undefined future time
It restricts salvation to the Mosaic Law period
questions.correctAnswer: It emphasizes that now is the accepted time for salvation, urging immediate response
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 6:1-2 highlights the present moment as the accepted time for salvation, aligning with the New Testament's teaching on the urgent call to repentance and faith.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do 2 Corinthians 6:9 and 6:10 teach about Christian suffering and spiritual wealth?
options: Suffering destroys spiritual life and wealth
Suffering and poverty can coexist with spiritual richness and joy
Spiritual wealth depends on material prosperity
questions.correctAnswer: Suffering and poverty can coexist with spiritual richness and joy
questions.explanation: Verses 6:9-10 describe Christians as 'dying, and behold, we live' and 'poor, yet making many rich,' teaching that external suffering does not preclude inner spiritual abundance.

questions.question: What doctrine about purity and separation from evil is taught by the synthesis of 2 Corinthians 6:17 and 6:14?
options: Believers are called to assimilate with unbelievers
Believers are commanded to come out and be separate, avoiding unequal yoking with unbelievers
Believers must tolerate the unclean to evangelize effectively
questions.correctAnswer: Believers are commanded to come out and be separate, avoiding unequal yoking with unbelievers
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 6:17 commands believers to separate from unclean things, while 6:14 warns against unequal yoking, jointly teaching the doctrine of holiness through separation.

questions.question: What doctrine concerning the nature of Christian ministry is taught by combining 2 Corinthians 6:7 and 6:8?
options: Ministry involves only honorable and easy tasks
Ministry entails facing both honor and dishonor, empowered by truth and righteousness
Ministers should avoid any form of deception
Ministry success depends on human wisdom alone
questions.correctAnswer: Ministry entails facing both honor and dishonor, empowered by truth and righteousness
questions.explanation: Verses 6:7-8 highlight ministers functioning by 'the word of truth' and 'the armour of righteousness' while enduring both 'honour and dishonour,' teaching the paradox of faithful ministry.

questions.question: What does 2 Corinthians 6:4-7 teach that counters the sceptical claim that Christian ministers only seek ease and popularity?
options: Ministers avoid suffering and hardship to maintain popularity
Ministers approve themselves through patience, kindness, and the Holy Ghost despite afflictions
Ministers rely on political power for success
Ministry is a path to worldly riches
questions.correctAnswer: Ministers approve themselves through patience, kindness, and the Holy Ghost despite afflictions
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 6:4-7 describes ministers enduring afflictions, showing longsuffering, kindness, and spiritual power, refuting the idea that ministry is about ease or popularity.

questions.question: What doctrine about the believer’s relationship to unbelievers is taught by 2 Corinthians 6:15?
options: Believers and unbelievers share equal spiritual concord
Christ has no concord with Belial, indicating spiritual opposition between believers and infidels
Believers should form spiritual partnerships with unbelievers
Believers are indistinguishable from infidels in spiritual matters
questions.correctAnswer: Christ has no concord with Belial, indicating spiritual opposition between believers and infidels
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 6:15 states 'what concord hath Christ with Belial?' illustrating the doctrinal truth of spiritual opposition between Christ and forces of evil, and thus between believers and infidels.

questions.question: What theological insight about the new covenant is taught in 2 Corinthians 6:16-18?
options: God dwells only in the Jerusalem temple
Believers collectively constitute the living temple where God dwells and promises sonship
The new covenant abolishes all separation from idols
God’s presence is distant from believers
questions.correctAnswer: Believers collectively constitute the living temple where God dwells and promises sonship
questions.explanation: Verses 6:16-18 teach that believers are the temple of the living God, where God dwells and promises to be their Father, reflecting new covenant realities beyond the old temple.

questions.question: What doctrine about God’s grace is taught by 2 Corinthians 6:1?
options: God’s grace can be received in vain if not properly responded to
God’s grace is always effective regardless of human response
Grace is only for the apostolic generation
Grace does not require human cooperation
questions.correctAnswer: God’s grace can be received in vain if not properly responded to
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 6:1 warns believers not to receive the grace of God in vain, teaching that grace requires a proper response to be effectual.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do 2 Corinthians 6:11 and 6:13 teach about the relationship between Paul and the Corinthians?
options: Paul is distant and unapproachable to the Corinthians
Paul expresses openness and invites mutual expansion of heart, reflecting a familial bond
Paul demands strict legalism without relational warmth
questions.correctAnswer: Paul expresses openness and invites mutual expansion of heart, reflecting a familial bond
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 6:11 and 6:13 describe Paul opening his mouth and heart to the Corinthians and urging them to be enlarged, indicating a warm, familial relationship.
